subject: Temporary capacity throttle & feature-flag access for summer pilot
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@mediphy.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@mediphy.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T10:02:00Z
Subject: Temporary capacity throttle & feature-flag access for summer pilot

Hi Ben,

Hope you had a good week. Quick ask from procurement and ops — we’re expecting a seasonal dip in July/Aug and would like to explore a temporary reduction in our reserved capacity for that window. High level: would you be open to a 40% reduction in our committed GPUs for a 60-day window with a billing credit and the option to auto-resume to full capacity at the end of August?

Two important constraints from our side:
- We need continued access to the premium feature set (the private model variant endpoints and the feature-flag gating) — engineers will still call those in the pilot.
- Compliance: the feature-flag change needs to be auditable and reversible (audit logs).

I attached our recent usage summary for context. Can you put forward an amendment that shows the economics (monthly credit, overage rates, reactivation terms) and any operational guards? We’re trying to avoid a long-term contract change — just a short amendment.

Thanks,
Ethan Cole
Head of Procurement | MediPhy
procurement@mediphy.com
[Attachment: summer_usage_report.csv (csv, 42KB)]

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@mediphy.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T15:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity throttle & feature-flag access for summer pilot

Ethan — thanks for the context and the report. We can absolutely do a short-term throttle; below is a pragmatic proposal we can put into an amendment. I’ll also loop in legal/ops (Lauren) for the auditability piece.

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 2027-07-01 -> 2027-08-29 (60 days)
- Capacity: 40% reduction in reserved throughput (committed GPU hours) during the term
- Billing: 25% credit applied to base reserved fee for the two-month window
- Overages: metered overage billed at a 10% discounted rate vs your normal overage price
- Feature access: premium endpoints and private variants remain enabled via a temporary entitlement (feature-flag) tied to your account — audit logs will be retained for 12 months
- Reactivation: one-time $2,000 reactivation fee to revert provisioning back to full capacity (to cover scheduling/placement churn)
- Guardrail: automatic resume to full capacity at 00:00 UTC on 2027-08-30 unless you opt out in writing

Next steps: I attached a draft amendment (proposed_amendment_v1.pdf). If this looks good to procurement/legal we can finalize and send for signature. If you need a deeper discount or to waive the reactivation fee, flag it and I’ll route to pricing.

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the numbers.

— Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: proposed_amendment_v1.pdf (pdf, 18KB)]

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@mediphy.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity throttle & feature-flag access for summer pilot

Looping in from pricing side. Ben — good start. Two suggestions to protect both parties while keeping the deal attractive:

1) Discount level: bump the credit to 30% (instead of 25%) given the contract churn and the fact that they will keep premium features live.
2) Reactivation fee: waive the $2,000 reactivation fee if MediPhy agrees to a short minimum usage guarantee (shortfall protection) equal to 50% of the reduced reserved fee for the 60-day term; if shortfall occurs, charge the difference. This avoids unpredictable provisioning costs for us while removing the upfront reactivation barrier for them.

Also recommend adding a rollback clause: if capacity utilization after reactivation exceeds 110% of reserved capacity for 14 consecutive days, we reserve the right to propose a temporary scale-up or consult on traffic shaping (not an automatic charge).

If that sounds reasonable I’ll update the numbers in the amendment and generate a DocuSign-ready version.

— Priyom Das
Director, Commercial Pricing | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@mediphy.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@mediphy.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity throttle & feature-flag access for summer pilot

Thanks Ben & Priyom — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few quick responses inline: 

- Credit: MediPhy can accept 25% if the reactivation fee is removed. If you require reactivation fee, we’d ask for a higher credit to compensate.
- Shortfall protection: we’re open to the shortfall clause (50%) but would prefer a token-based floor instead of a dollar shortfall (easier for our finance).
- Feature flags / audit: must be controlled by our SREs with the ability to open a support ticket to revert changes; audit logs need to include actor, timestamp, and change reason for compliance.

We’ve attached a signed redline (minimal edits) to the proposed amendment — see attached PDF. Assuming we can remove the reactivation fee and preserve a 25% credit + token-floor shortfall, we can approve for signature this week.

Ethan Cole
Head of Procurement | MediPhy
procurement@mediphy.com
[Attachment: signed_redline_amendment.pdf (pdf, 23KB)]

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@mediphy.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity throttle & feature-flag access for summer pilot

Thanks all — legal and ops reviewed the redline. We can accept the following final terms: 

- 60-day throttle (2027-07-01 -> 2027-08-29) with 25% credit to reserved fee
- Reactivation fee: waived as requested by MediPhy
- Shortfall protection: token-floor equal to 50% of the reduced reserved token allocation (we will define the token-to-hour mapping in the amendment)
- Feature-flag access: enabled for MediPhy’s SREs; changes will be auditable (actor, timestamp, reason) and require a ticket for support-assisted reverts
- SLA note: during throttle window, we will maintain the same support coverage but warn that provisioning lead times for scale-up may be up to 24-48 hours depending on capacity availability; this is documented in the amendment

I’ll finalize the amendment with the token-floor mapping and push to DocuSign (link to follow). Ben — please confirm the HubSpot deal and I’ll attach the DocuSign envelope.

— Lauren Bishop
Head of Contracts & Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4821; DocuSign to follow
